name: Generative Antibody and Protein Design
blurb: AI that designs new antibodies and proteins from scratch.
title: Generative Antibody and Protein Design
answer: Generative models now propose antibodies and proteins that have never existed, and some companies report double digit experimental hit rates for fully de novo designs, far above traditional screening. Venture money has followed: Chai Discovery raised $70 million in August 2025 and $130 million in December 2025.

reading.body:
Generative protein design has produced antibodies now in a phase 3 trial, which is the strongest evidence yet that the method yields real drug candidates.

The pattern is a shift from screening to generation. Traditional discovery searches existing or mutated molecules for one that binds a target. Generative models propose sequences that have never existed, and Chai Discovery reports double digit experimental hit rates for fully de novo antibody designs. Generate:Biomedicines has carried one such design, GB-0895, into a phase 3 trial, which moves the claim from benchmark to clinic.

For AI specifically, the money and the trial both point the same direction. Chai Discovery raised $70 million in August 2025 and $130 million in December 2025, with the second round citing the hit rates. Capital at that scale follows demonstrated output, not promise. The compute behind these models is a smaller share of the cost than the wet lab work that validates each design, so the binding constraint here is experimental capacity rather than chips or power.

What the data does not cover is how these hit rates were measured, on which targets, or whether they hold outside the company reporting them. It names one trial and one company's funding, not the field. Treat the numbers as claims until they reproduce on blinded targets.

sections.body: Treat vendor hit rates as claims until they hold on your own targets. Ask for prospective results on blinded targets before committing.
